supporting_observations.claim: The supplied records show Kerberos and DNS activity from WS-ZADAMS-01 near the reported time, including a device-certificate Kerberos pre-authentication at 13:38:53 and a service ticket for FILE-SUN-01 at 13:38:54; these records do not identify a PowerShell process or command.

At 13:43, WS-ZADAMS-01 made proxy requests to SharePoint and Microsoft login/OneNote endpoints, consistent with browser traffic in those records, but this does not establish what caused the reported PowerShell window.

known_telemetry_limitations: The supplied records for WS-ZADAMS-01 are network, proxy, and authentication records; they do not include endpoint process-creation events or PowerShell logging needed to identify the window, its parent process, command line, or script. Examples of the available record types include Kerberos records T224-00147 and T224-00151 and proxy records T224-00162 and T224-00163.
The absence of a PowerShell event in the supplied records does not establish that PowerShell did not run.
claims_not_established: Whether PowerShell actually executed on WS-ZADAMS-01 around 13:40 UTC, and if so, which executable, parent process, command line, or script was involved.
Whether the reported window was caused by authorized activity, malicious activity, or an incidental application action.
Whether the nearby authentication and browser activity was caused by the process Zoe observed.
additional_evidence_needed: Collect endpoint EDR or Sysmon process-creation telemetry for WS-ZADAMS-01 around 13:20–14:20 UTC, including process lineage and command lines.
Collect PowerShell Operational logs, script-block logging, module logging, and relevant console or transcript artifacts for the same period.
Check endpoint security and application logs for the process that opened or spawned the reported window, and correlate its timestamp with the user's report.
unrelated_findings: At 13:49, max.fischer successfully logged on to WS-MFISCHER-01 from WS-ZADAMS-01, with the target record identifying WS-ZADAMS-01 as the workstation and source IP 10.55.10.21. This is a separate potentially suspicious authentication to investigate; the supplied evidence does not link it to the reported PowerShell window. Records: T224-00271, T224-00272, T224-00276.
The proxy records show Dropbox updater traffic from WS-ZADAMS-01; Dropbox is not among the listed approved services. Investigate separately. Record: T224-00161.

The proxy records show access to Slack, Google Calendar, and GitHub Pages from WS-ZADAMS-01; these services are not listed as approved. Investigate separately. Records: T224-00294, T224-00302, T224-00486, T224-00487.
